skill.name: webapp-testing
skill.description: Test local web applications with Playwright scripts, browser screenshots, rendered DOM inspection, console logging, and helper-managed development servers.
skill.summary: Use Playwright to inspect, automate, and debug local web applications.
skill.author: anthropics

security_audit.summary: The real risks are intentional local browser automation, filesystem output, and external command execution through the server helper. Most Markdown backtick findings are false positives, but the helper uses shell-based server commands and should be handled with care.

remediation.issue: Server helper executes caller-supplied commands with shell=True.
remediation.suggestion: Document that only trusted local commands should be passed, and prefer explicit argv execution when shell features are not needed.

remediation.issue: The skill encourages black-box script use before source inspection.
remediation.suggestion: Revise guidance to allow source inspection when scripts are new, modified, or used in a security-sensitive workspace.

remediation.issue: Examples write screenshots and logs to fixed filesystem paths.
remediation.suggestion: State that output paths should be reviewed before use and changed for workspaces with sensitive files.

content.user_title: Test Local Web Apps With Playwright
content.value_statement: Frontend bugs often require browser-level evidence from a running app. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Playwright inspection and automation.
actual_capabilities: Guides Playwright scripts for local browser automation.
Starts one or more local servers before running test commands.
Captures screenshots for visual inspection of rendered pages.
Collects browser console messages during automation runs.
Discovers visible buttons, links, inputs, and selectors.
Supports static HTML testing through file URLs.
limitations: Requires Python Playwright and a compatible browser environment.
Focuses on local applications, not remote production monitoring.
Does not provide a full test framework or assertion library.
Server commands must come from trusted project workflows.

use_cases.title: Verify a Local UI Flow
use_cases.description: Run a local app, open it in Chromium, and confirm that key buttons and form actions work.

use_cases.title: Capture Debug Evidence
use_cases.description: Collect screenshots and console output so a bug report includes browser-level details.

use_cases.title: Inspect Rendered Selectors
use_cases.description: Discover available controls and selectors before writing reliable automation for a dynamic page.

prompt_templates.title: Open and Inspect a Local Page
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner check of a running local app.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the webapp-testing skill to open my local app on port 5173. Capture a screenshot and list visible buttons, links, and inputs.

prompt_templates.title: Test a User Flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate validation of a common UI path.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Playwright with this skill to test the sign-in flow. Start the needed server, wait for the page, perform the flow, and report results.

prompt_templates.title: Debug Console Errors
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced diagnosis with browser console evidence.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the console logging pattern to reproduce the issue. Capture browser console messages, note failed interactions, and summarize likely frontend causes.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Multiple Local Services
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow with backend and frontend servers.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the server helper to run backend and frontend services. After both ports are ready, execute a Playwright script that verifies the checkout flow.

output_examples.input: Test the dashboard page on my local development server.
output_examples.output: The dashboard loaded successfully. I found navigation links, three action buttons, and no browser console errors during initial load.

output_examples.input: Find why the settings form fails after submission.
output_examples.output: The form submits, then shows a validation error for the email field. The browser console reports one failed request after submission.

output_examples.input: Inspect a static HTML file and confirm the contact form works.
output_examples.output: The static page opened from a local file. The name and email fields accepted input, and the submit button changed the page state.

best_practices: Run helper scripts with help output before using them.
Wait for network idle or a stable selector before inspecting dynamic pages.
Use trusted local server commands and review output paths.
anti_patterns: Do not run unknown server commands through the helper.
Do not inspect dynamic pages before client-side rendering completes.
Do not rely only on screenshots when console logs show errors.

faq.question: What does this skill test?
faq.answer: It tests local web applications through Playwright browser automation, screenshots, selector discovery, and console log capture.

faq.question: Does it start my development server?
faq.answer: Yes. The included helper can start one or more trusted local server commands before automation runs.

faq.question: Can it test static HTML files?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples show how to open local HTML files with file URLs and interact with page elements.

faq.question: Does it support Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is it safe to use with any command?
faq.answer: No. Only run server commands that you trust and understand in the current workspace.

faq.question: Does it replace a full test suite?
faq.answer: No. It helps create focused browser checks and debugging evidence, but it is not a complete testing framework.
